note: Authored by reading Tafsir al-Tabari in English against the reader's modern translation. Each phrase carries the app's own words for that piece of the verse, a plain modern English line of my own, the Arabic of the piece, and the numbered paragraphs of the commentary that speak of it.

phrases.translation: I do swear by this city ˹of Mecca˺—
phrases.text: God swears by this city, and the commentators agree that Mecca is meant.

phrases.translation: even though you ˹O Prophet˺ are subject to abuse in this city—
phrases.text: Tabari reads this as: you are free in this city. You are unhindered there, and what you do there is allowed you. On the day he entered Mecca this was given to the Prophet, who killed Ibn Khatal there while the man clung to the cloths of the Kaaba. No one after him is allowed to kill in the sanctuary.

phrases.translation: and by every parent and ˹their˺ child
phrases.text: The commentators differed: some said it means every father and the child he begot, some said Adam and his offspring, and some said Abraham and what he begot. Tabari keeps it general, because there is no sound proof that limits it.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We have created humankind in ˹constant˺ struggle
phrases.text: This answers the oath. The commentators differed: some said man was made for heaviness and toil, and man is found only struggling with the affairs of this world and the next. Some said he was created upright. Tabari takes the toil, because that is the well-known meaning of the word among the Arabs.

phrases.translation: Do they think that no one has power over them
phrases.text: This was revealed about a strong man of the Banu Jumah. Does he, in his strength and power, think that no one will overpower and overcome him? God is the one who overpowers him.
phrases.ar: أَيَحۡسَبُ أَن لَّن يَقۡدِرَ عَلَيۡهِ أَحَدٞ

phrases.translation: boasting, “I have wasted enormous wealth!”
phrases.text: The strong and obstinate man says: I have squandered a great fortune in enmity against the Prophet, and he is lying in that. The word means what is heaped up, one thing upon another.

phrases.translation: Do they think that no one sees them
phrases.text: Does the man who says he has squandered a great fortune suppose that no one saw him while he was spending it? Qatada says: you will surely be asked about this wealth, where you got it and where you spent it.

phrases.translation: Have We not given them two eyes
phrases.text: God made him two eyes with which he sees the proofs against him, and a tongue with which he says what he likes, and two lips. These are favours of God, one after another.

phrases.translation: a tongue, and two lips
phrases.text: A tongue and two lips, so that you may give thanks for them.

phrases.translation: and shown them the two ways ˹of right and wrong˺
phrases.text: We have shown him the two ways, and a way is a road that runs upward. The commentators differed: some said the way of good and the way of evil, and some that it means the two breasts. Tabari takes the two ways, because God counted only His guidance to the good way among His favours.

phrases.translation: If only they had attempted the challenging path ˹of goodness instead˺
phrases.text: He has not climbed the steep pass so as to traverse it. The commentators said the steep pass is a mountain in Hell, some said it is Hell itself, and Qatada said it is a hard ascent that you climb by obeying God.

phrases.translation: And what will make you realize what ˹attempting˺ the challenging path is
phrases.text: What has made you know, O Muhammad, what the steep pass is? And then God explains it: the storming of it and the way to take it are the works that follow.

phrases.translation: It is to free a slave
phrases.text: Freeing a neck from slavery. The Prophet said that whoever frees a believing slave has that as his ransom from the Fire, and that for every bone of the one freed God sets a bone of the freed man's bones as a protection against the Fire.

phrases.translation: or to give food in times of famine
phrases.text: Or feeding on a day of hunger. The commentators say the day of famine is a day on which food is longed for, and that the word means hunger itself.
phrases.ar: أَوۡ إِطۡعَٰمٞ فِي يَوۡمٖ ذِي مَسۡغَبَةٖ

phrases.translation: to an orphaned relative
phrases.text: On that day of hunger, feeding a small child who has no father, one of your own relatives. The word for relative means one of your blood relations.

phrases.translation: or to a poor person in distress
phrases.text: Or a needy man in distress. The commentators differed: some said it is the one who has no shelter but the dust, some the one in severe need whatever his state, and some the one with a large family and nothing to give them. Tabari takes the one whose poverty has brought him down to the dust.

phrases.translation: and—above all—to be one of those who have faith and urge each other to perseverance and urge each other to compassion
phrases.text: And above all, to be among those who believed in God and His messenger, who urged one another to be patient over what befell them for God's sake, and who urged one another to compassion, which Ibn Abbas says is compassion toward people.
phrases.ar: ثُمَّ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِٱلصَّبۡرِ وَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِٱلۡمَرۡحَمَةِ

phrases.translation: These are the people of the right
phrases.text: Those who did these works, the freeing of slaves, the feeding of the orphan and the rest, are the people of the right hand, who on the day of resurrection are led to the Garden.

phrases.translation: As for those who deny Our signs, they are the people of the left
phrases.text: Those who disbelieved in God's proofs and arguments, the scriptures and the messengers, are the people of the left hand, who are led to the left side on the day of resurrection.
phrases.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا هُمۡ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلۡمَشۡـَٔمَةِ

phrases.translation: The Fire will be sealed over them
phrases.text: Over them on the day of resurrection is the Fire of Hell, shut tightly closed. There is no light in it, no relief, and no escape from it for ever.
